data.name: Girija
data.gender_notes: Girija is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Goddess of mountains and mother of Lord Ganesha
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Girija is the name of the goddess Parvati, the wife of Lord Shiva. She is also known as Girija or Girijaa, the mother of Lord Ganesha. This name signifies strength, stability, and nurturing love. The name Girija carries the meaning “Goddess of mountains and mother of Lord Ganesha” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Girija usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of mountains and mother of lord ganesha and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine, motherhood, and the strength of nature.
data.etymology: Girija belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of mountains and mother of Lord Ganesha.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Girija total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Girija has significant cultural importance in Hinduism, as it is the name of one of the primary goddesses in the Hindu pantheon. Parvati, also known as Girija, is widely revered and celebrated, particularly during the Navratri festival. Her stories of love, devotion, and motherhood are an integral part of Hindu mythology and folklore and continue to influence Hindu art, literature, and culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Girija or Parvati is considered the embodiment of divine feminine energy, representing unconditional love, strength, and nurturing. Her name signifies the all-encompassing power of the mother universe, who is capable of creating and destroying, loving and punishing. Girija's story of love and devotion toward Lord Shiva and her role as the mother of Lord Ganesha represents the fulfilling aspect of motherhood and the importance of maintaining balance and harmony within relationships.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Girija, derived from the Sanskrit word 'Girija' meaning 'Mountain' or 'Lady of the Mountain', symbolizes the divine feminine energy embodied in the form of Parvati, the consort of Shiva. It signifies strength, stability, and the nurturing power of the earth.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Girija is a name of Parvati, the consort of Shiva in Hindu mythology. The name Girija carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
